title: Telemetry-driven adapter heuristics for OpenAI Responses mapping and runtime selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When routing customer traffic to our OpenAI Responses compatibility layer we see varying classes of fidelity loss depending on (1) streaming vs buffered mode, (2) function/tool-calling semantics, and (3) structured-output enforcement. These failures show up as subtle behavioral deltas (token re-ordering, missing toolcall events, truncated structured objects) that are not well captured by our current binary contract tests.

Goals:
- Define a telemetry-driven heuristic system that chooses the most appropriate adapter mapping at runtime (conservative mapping, permissive mapping, or inline translation) based on observed signals.
- Create a lossiness score and provenance tracing model so that we can detect, surface, and automatically degrade traffic when adapter-induced regressions exceed thresholds.
- Ship an evaluation harness + contract test suite that exercises streaming+toolcalling+structured-output combinations and can be run in CI and as post-deploy canaries.

Why this is different: Instead of a single static "responses->redwood" translator, we will maintain a small set of runtime adapters and an instrumented decision layer that selects adapters per-request (or per-session) based on telemetry (latency, delta-score, error types, customer policy). This reduces blast radius and lets us conservatively handle edge cases while retaining best-effort parity for most traffic.
runbook: 1) Instrument token-level events and correlate with adapter decisions (stored in trace metadata). 2) Compute a per-request lossiness_score (0..1) using heuristics described below. 3) If lossiness_score > 0.7 and customer policy == strict, route to fallback hosted model variant. 4) Log detailed provenance to secure audit stream for customers with Private deployments. 5) Canary: enable telemetry heuristics behind a feature flag for 5% traffic, monitor for 72h before ramping.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for each adapter mapping (buffered, streaming-pass-through, structured-wrapper).
- Contract fuzz harness that replays real production traces with mutated events to validate lossiness detection.
- Binary compatibility suite run on PRs + nightly run with synthetic trace combos for streaming+toolcalls.
- Canary gate: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback if error-rate or regression-signal spikes > 2x baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Lossiness score computed for 100% of adapted requests in canary, with per-route histograms available in Console.
2) Two new adapters merged: streaming-pass-through and structured-wrapper (both behind flags).
3) CI contract suite passes on PRs and nightly; mean regression signal in canary < 0.5% vs baseline.
4) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with example patch-level mappings.
notes_and_decisions: 2025-02-12: Decided to implement three adapter modes: pass-through (low-latency, high-risk), wrapper (ensures structured JSON validity), and conservative-translate (best-effort semantic mapping).

2025-02-18: Chose a lightweight lossiness heuristic combining: missing-toolcall-events ratio, structural-field-drop rate, token-rewrite entropy, and streaming-event-suppression. Each signal is normalized and combined with weights (see design doc).

2025-02-24: Trade-off: embedding more logic into the adapter increases per-request CPU; mitigated by caching adapter decisions per-session and limiting heavy translations to 5% of tokens (configurable).
2025-03-01: Security review flagged provenance storage location for Private customers; plan to encrypt traces with customer KMS (follow-up: ENG-860130).
